title: Automation Queue Backlog Indicator
dataSources: Home Assistant state/logbook events (`homeassistant:event`), Homey flow/insights (`homey:flow`), SmartThings events (`smartthings:event`), Hubitat/openHAB logs, Node-RED flow events (`nodered:event`).
app: Home Assistant / Homey / SmartThings / Hubitat / openHAB event streams via MQTT, webhooks, and REST - forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=homeassistant:event event_type=automation_triggered
| stats count as triggered_runs, avg(queue_depth) as avg_queue_depth by automation
| where avg_queue_depth>1 OR triggered_runs>20
| sort - avg_queue_depth
description: Surfaces automations that are frequently queued up behind earlier runs, a subtle sign that their actions are taking too long or firing too often.
value: Queueing is how a responsive home starts feeling sticky; a backlog indicator tells you which automations need debouncing, splitting, or faster actions.
implementation: Forward queue-depth or parallel-run metadata for each automation trigger; review slow burners before they become user-visible lag.
visualization: Table of automations by average queue depth and trigger volume.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces when certain routines are piling up on top of each other instead of finishing before the next one starts.
